newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bankers want lower reserve requirements.
newsitem.headline: Polish bankers want lower reserve requirements.

text.p: The Polish Banking Association (ZNP) wants the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to lower obligatory reserve requirements on commercial banks, the association's president said on Wednesday.
Andrzej Szukalski told a news conference that falling inflation created room for a required reserves reduction despite quickly growing credit action.
"If (year-on-year) inflation is falling...then the burden from required reserves is too high," Szukalski said.
The central bank had said that a rise in required reserves could not be ruled out as a tool for further curbing credit growth, which increased 8.5 percent in the first quarter alone.
"We have different opinions (than the NBP) on credit action. We think that increasing credit is a good sign as long as the credit is safe," Szukalski said.

On February 28 the central bank increased obligatory reserves on zloty call deposits by three points to 20 percent and doubled the requirement on foreign currency deposits to four percent in order to slow credit growth, especially consumption credit to households.
In 1996 credit to the non-financial sector increased by 42.7 percent and credit to households rose by 108.5 percent.
